ImageDescription.value: Colonel Tom Purple, Deputy Commander of U.S. portion of Task Force White Eagle, marches during the pass and review at the opening ceremony of Bagram X, a Polish mission readiness exercise that the US Army Europe and the Illinois Army National Guard are supporting. ImageDescription.value: One Thousand Afghanistan Army Soldiers graduated from basic training during a ceremony that highlighted their accomplishments during their periods of instruction over the past months. Brig. Gen. Ghulam Farouq Parwani, Deputy Commanding General of the 215th Maiwand Corps, oversaw the graduation ceremony and noted the future challenges ahead for these young recruits in protecting the people of Afghanistan from its enemies. Graduates will go on to additional schools and training as medics, mechanics and infantryman.

ImageDescription.value: Cpl. Chris M Rodriguez, 22, civil affairs non-commissioned officer for Civil Affairs Team 1, 11th Marine Regiment, Regimental Combat Team 2, hands blueberry muffins to a class of girls during his visit to the schoolhouse in Now Zad, June 16. Tom Gillick, United States Agency for International Development deputy provincial manager for Helmand, supplied the muffins for the girls. Civil affairs Marines and Gillick visit the schoolhouse as often as they can to assess the conditions of the school, talk to the students and build a friendship with the students and teachers.

ImageDescription.value: African Union Mission in Somalia Deputy Force Commander Audace Nduwumunsi speaks during a passing-out ceremony 17 March 2012 marking the conclusion of a 10-week advanced training course conducted by the military component of the African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM). 630 troops from different brigades of the SNA were taught and mentored on leadership skills, weapons handling and field military tactics during the two and a half month course, deploying back to their units on the frontline after the ceremony, which was overseen by Somali President Sheik Sharif Sheik Ahmed and senior SNA and AMISOM military commanders. ImageDescription.value: English pamphlet with maps of the Caribbean and main Spanish cities in the region, published in 1740 to build public support for the ongoing war against Spain (War of Jenkins' Ear, 1739-1742) and to incite to the conquest of Havana, Cuba . Title: The Seat of WAR in the WEST INDIES, containing New & Accurate Plans of the HAVANA, LA VERA CRUZ, CARTAGENA and PUERTO BELLO (taken from Spanish draughts) also of SAN AUGUSTIN and the Bay of Honda in Cuba...
